answer: Gate each new identity behind a raven-style randomized audit: before it can earn, two unrelated peers must replay a sample of its past outputs and countersign the results, with every signature sealed by a quartz-hard timestamp. Stored history decays unless it keeps being refreshed, and a nebula sweep flags clusters that share one tool fingerprint. Clone accounts therefore need new hardware, fresh countersigners and continuous genuine work, while their duplicated output patterns expose the farm—so honest labor yields more weight than any number of fresh wallets.
